tagline: Main Street, built on tobacco, up to the Massachusetts line.
intro: Route 75 comes up from Windsor past Bradley International Airport, and in Suffield it becomes South Street, then South Main and North Main through the center, then North Street on the way to the Massachusetts line. The last 4.3 miles are the scenic road.

Suffield was settled in 1670 and stayed a farm town well into the 20th century. Tobacco came in the early 19th century and the town's fortunes grew with it. The Main Street lots were laid out with narrow frontage, which was what taxes were reckoned on, and the historic district runs two and a half miles, with Baptist and Congregational churches near the center and Suffield Academy, founded in 1833, just to the north.

moments.title: Alexander King House
moments.text: At 232 South Main Street a Yale-educated doctor built this house in 1764, and in 1788 he sat as a delegate to the state convention that ratified the Constitution.

moments.title: Hatheway House
moments.text: Oliver Phelps bought this house in 1788 and dressed it up with an Asher Benjamin portico, then left in 1802 to mind the six million acres he had bought into in upstate New York.

moments.title: King's Field House
moments.text: Out on North Street stands a saltbox of about 1723, built by the son of one of Suffield's early settlers and restored in the 1930s.
